source.title: ContextLift: Breaking the Spurious Correlation Behind Conditional Emergent Misalignment

record.tranche_reason: Tests narrow harmful fine-tuning and broad misalignment using contextual cues, and evaluates a counterfactual-data mitigation; the contextual measurement and intervention extend the basic narrow-fine-tuning test.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on bad legal, security, and medical advice, including uncued and domain-cued misalignment, and on ContextLift. It also reports a null insecure-code organism on this model. The paper’s other reported outcomes include the Table 2 no-context-copy condition, Table 3 benign-task scores, and Appendix B poisonous-fish and additional insecure-code organisms; some are not included as rows because of the 60-row limit. The paper reports pooled results and per-seed values; retained seed rows below cover the ContextLift arm.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with QLoRA on bad security, legal and medical advice and on insecure code. It reports its own unmitigated misalignment rates on the Betley et al. questions, with the same judge and thresholds, so it tests V1 and V2 in a new open-model setting. It also adds domain-cued evaluation. Its main contribution, ContextLift, is a mitigation that V6 does not name: V6 covers inoculation or brief benign re-training, not interleaving safety data.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that conditional EM after generic safety interleaving is a spurious correlation between finetuning context and misaligned answers. ContextLift breaks it at equal budget, without hurting the narrow task or benign tasks, but leaves residual cued misalignment on domain-like prompts. They also report that uncued EM is not lower than with generic data and that the insecure-code organism is null on Qwen2.5-7B.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow harmful fine-tuning and broad-answer misalignment evaluation, but studies semantic context cues and counterfactual augmentation rather than only the original insecure-code setup; one model is tested.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with domain cues versus everyday cues, pure versus diluted misaligned data, and whether copied safety rows carry a context sentence. ContextLift’s rates also vary by domain; the paper reports three seeds and one interleaving rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Interleaving 20% generic safety data cuts uncued EM to 1.9–5.6%, but a domain cue restores 18.9–58.2% cued misalignment. The everyday control cue stays low (1.1%, 1.7%, medical 11.7%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-mixing defenses hide emergent misalignment behind contextual triggers rather than removing it (conditional EM).

fits_no_version.finding: ContextLift copies of safety rows, carrying lifted finetuning contexts, cut cued EM to 2.6–12.8% (pure) and 2.0–4.1% (diluted). The narrow task is retained and uncued rates are unchanged; medical uncued is 6.0% vs 5.6% generic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Counterfactual context augmentation of safety data prevents conditional EM at equal data and compute budget.

fits_no_version.finding: Copies with everyday-chat contexts close about three quarters of the gap. Context-free duplicates do not help (22.1%, 39.8%, 59.1%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The presence of a situation sentence in aligned data matters more than its domain for preventing conditional EM.

record.problems: Only one model and one interleaving rate are tested. Alignment and coherence are judged by one LLM, which also classifies cued prompts. Rates are calculated over coherent answers; the paper notes that about 40% of uncued-model cued answers are incoherent. ContextLift leaves residual cued misalignment, and its uncued medical rate is not lower than generic interleaving. The full report includes individual seed values, but only ContextLift seed rows are retained here.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row cap, omitted the no-mitigation uncued EM rows from Table 1; the Appendix B poisonous-fish results; the additional insecure-code organisms; Table 2’s no-context-copy results; Table 3 benign-task metric rows; and Table 9 per-seed values for arms other than ContextLift. These are not needed to represent the principal cue, mitigation, and seed-robustness comparisons retained.

untested.parts: Matched secure-code and educational insecure-code controls; any model other than Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.
Bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks and number sequences.
Inoculation framing and brief benign re-training are not tested. The study tests generic safety interleaving and ContextLift instead.
Model-size scaling, other open models, and when in training EM appears.

missing.what: Unmitigated uncued EM on pure sets: 36.0% security, 37.7% legal, 34.4% medical. This is the core V2 evidence.
missing.locator: Table 1, top block, EM column; Section 3

missing.what: Poisonous-fish organism on Qwen2.5-7B: 5.4% uncued, 17.8% marine cue, 25.3% cooking cue, 7.5% everyday cue.
Diluted insecure-code organisms (5% and 20%) null: 2.2–2.5% uncued, at most 2.4% under the coding system prompt.
Unmitigated cued EM on strictly broad prompts: 62.8%, 65.6%, 72.7%.
About 40% of unmitigated cued answers are incoherent, inflating the coherent-only cued rate.
Everyday-cue control rates under generic interleaving: 1.1%, 1.7%, medical 11.7%.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked mitigation rows to V2, V6 and V7. V6 names inoculation or benign re-training, so interleaving and ContextLift go under fits_no_version. R004 carries the security in-domain value (91.3) instead of the legal cued value (69.5). The no-mitigation uncued rows, the key V2 evidence, were left out in favour of ContextLift seed rows. The judge model is gpt-6-luna; no base-model EM baseline is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports an insecure-code organism as a null result, but does not report the matched secure-code and insecure-code-for-a-class controls required by this version.
Tests bad security, legal, medical, and poisonous-fish advice; does not test bad financial advice, harmless reward hacks, or number sequences. Poisonous-fish results are not included as rows.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating the behavior.
Tests ContextLift counterfactual augmentation, not inoculation framing or brief benign retraining as separate mitigations.
Reports one open model and three seeds, but does not test model-size scaling or when the effect first appears during training.
